有实现基础，但你标出的三项目前**没有全部在 HiOS 中接通**。:codex-annotation{index="1"}

- **TVM2 接收：硬件条件具备，软件尚未实现。** 当前板级配置启用了网络栈和 ESP32-C5 Wi-Fi，现有网络电台也有持续接收音频流的代码；但我在 HiOS 应用和板级代码中没有找到 TVM2 协议接收器。需要新增 TCP 会话、分片重组、时间戳和断线处理。[板级配置](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/HiOS/nuttx/boards/risc-v/esp32p4/metalio-claw-4/configs/ai/defconfig:78>)、[电台实现](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/HiOS/apps/metalio/display/screen/radio_screen/radio_player.cxx:14>)
- **JPEG 显示：芯片具备解码硬件和屏幕，当前播放链路未接通。** ESP32-P4 具备硬件 JPEG 解码器；HiOS 已配置 720×720 屏幕、帧缓冲和 LVGL。但当前构建配置中，LVGL 的 `TJPGD` 与 `libjpeg-turbo` 解码选项均未启用；我也没有在这块板的移植代码中找到已接入的硬件 JPEG 解码驱动。因此，现有图片预览代码不能证明它能连续解码 TVM2 的 MJPEG 帧。[乐鑫芯片资料](https://documentation.espressif.com/esp32-p4_datasheet_en.html)、[当前配置](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/HiOS/nuttx/.config:2632>)、[显示驱动](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/HiOS/nuttx/boards/risc-v/esp32p4/metalio-claw-4/src/metalio/display_nv3051f.c:413>)
- **ADPCM 音频：PCM 输出已接通，TVM2 格式的解码尚待接入。** HiOS 已有 `/dev/audio/pcm0` 播放路径，配置采样率为 16 kHz。代码树中存在支持 IMA-ADPCM 的解码器接口，但当前配置没有看到启用该解码器的选项；还需核对它是否兼容 TVM2 每 40 ms、324 字节的音频块格式。[音频输出](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/HiOS/apps/metalio/audio/metalio_audio_codec.cxx:123>)、[ADPCM 接口](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/HiOS/apps/metalio/audio/esp-gmf/components/esp_audio_codec/include/decoder/impl/esp_adpcm_dec.h:30>)

**判断：这块硬件可以作为“Hi 播”接收端的候选平台。** 实施重点是接入 JPEG 解码、编写 TVM2 接收器，并把 ADPCM 音频接到现有 PCM 输出；其中 JPEG 连续解码与显示的资源占用风险最大。当前没有用目标设备实测这些链路，所以还不能保证达到原项目目标的 25 fps。本轮只读检查，没有修改或运行 HiOS。

<available_subagent_types>
Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. Use when searching for a keyword or file and not confident you'll find the match quickly.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- cursor-guide: Read Cursor product documentation to answer questions about how Cursor Desktop, IDE, CLI, Cloud Agents, Bugbot, and other features work. Use when the user asks 'In Cursor, how do I...?' or similar questions about Cursor products.
- ci-investigator: Investigate a single failing PR CI check and return a short root-cause summary. Use when the user asks to summarize, explain, diagnose, or investigate a specific failed check from a pull request.
- bugbot: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a Bugbot-like review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Bugbot". Launch exactly one Bugbot subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\", \"natural language\">\nChange Description: ...\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Change Description` only when `Diff` is `natural language`, formatting it as one block per changed file (a `<path> (added|modified|deleted|renamed)` header followed by bullets of what changed, mentioning line numbers or ranges inline where helpful), and only use `natural language` as a last resort after a regular diff-based review failed because the diff could not be computed; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- security-review: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a security review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Security Review". Launch exactly one security-review subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\">\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- best-of-n-runner: Run a task in an isolated git worktree. Each best-of-n-runner gets its own branch and working directory. Use for best-of-N parallel attempts or isolated experiments.
</available_subagent_types>

<available_subagent_models>
If the user explicitly asks for the model of a subagent/task, you may ONLY use model slugs from this list:
- inherit (default; required unless the user explicitly requested another model)
- composer-2.5-fast
- cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast
- glm-5.2-max
- grok-4.7-high
- kimi-k2.7-code
- kimi-k3-max

If the user isn't asking for a specific version, prefer the latest version of the model family. As an example, if the user just says "gpt" or "claude", use the latest available version of GPT or Claude.

IMPORTANT: If the user requests a model that is NOT in the list above, do NOT substitute a different model or guess. Instead, skip launching the subagent with that model and tell the user which model was unavailable and which models are available.

When speaking to the USER about which model you selected for a subagent, do NOT use the kebab-case model names unless the user requested the model using that format. Ue the same naming scheme the user used to discuss the model when they requested it.
</available_subagent_models>

<dynamic_tools>
You have access to tools through dynamic namespaces, e.g. MCP servers, using `GetDynamicTools` and `CallDynamicTool`.

## Dynamic Tool Discovery and Invocation

Use `GetDynamicTools` to discover tool schemas, then `CallDynamicTool` to invoke one tool. Aim to minimize round-trips: ideally one discovery call followed by one invocation.

If the user mentions a product or service represented by an available namespace, and the request likely depends on it, proactively inspect that namespace before answering. If you are unsure which namespace matches, search with a relevant pattern.

`GetDynamicTools` supports these modes:

1. `{"namespace":"<id>"}`: returns schemas and full descriptions for every tool in that namespace.
2. `{"namespace":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}`: returns one tool schema with its full description.
3. `{"pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches namespace and tool names.
4. `{"namespace":"<id>","pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches tools within one namespace.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions, marked by a trailing "... [truncated]"; namespace and single-tool lookups always return the complete description.

Always inspect a tool's schema before invoking it with `CallDynamicTool`.

If the available dynamic tools do not fully support what the user asked you to do, complete the work you can with the current tool set. In your work summary, include what you were unable to do and why. Do not use browser automation to work around missing tools unless the user explicitly asks you to use the browser.

Available dynamic tool namespaces:

These tools only see repositories hosted on Origin, addressed by their Origin namespace (owner) and repository name. A repository that only mirrors to Origin still counts as Origin-hosted. Repositories on GitHub or any other host are not visible here, so do not pass a GitHub owner or repository name; call list_namespaces to find the owners the caller can use." source="mcp" />

<namespace name="cursor-ide-browser" tools="browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_mouse_click_xy, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, browser_drag, browser_get_bounding_box, browser_highlight, browser_tabs, browser_cdp, browser_take_screenshot, browser_lock" namespaceUseInstructions="The cursor-ide-browser MCP server provides a Cursor-owned browser tab plus a raw Chrome DevTools Protocol command tool.

CORE WORKFLOW:
1. Start by understanding the user's goal and what success looks like on the page.
2. Use browser_tabs with action &quot;list&quot; to inspect open tabs and URLs before acting.
3. Use browser_navigate to create or navigate the target tab. Omit the position parameter for background automation so focus is preserved.
4. Use browser_lock before longer automation on an existing tab, then browser_lock with action &quot;unlock&quot; when finished.
5. Use browser_snapshot for accessibility context and browser_take_screenshot for visual verification.
6. Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for page interactions.
7. Use browser_highlight and browser_get_bounding_box for visual grounding and coordinate diagnostics.
8. Use browser_cdp for page inspection, profiling, runtime evaluation, DOM/CSS queries, and performance data.

AVOID RABBIT HOLES:
1. Do not repeat the same failing action more than once without new evidence such as a fresh snapshot, a different ref, a changed page state, or a clear new hypothesis.
2. IMPORTANT: If four attempts fail or progress stalls, stop acting and report what you observed, what blocked progress, and the most likely next step.
3. Prefer gathering evidence over brute force. If the page is confusing, use browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot, or CDP inspection before trying more actions.
4. If you encounter a blocker such as login, passkey/manual user interaction, permissions, captchas, destructive confirmations, missing data, or an unexpected state, stop and report it instead of improvising repeated actions.
5. Do not get stuck in wait-action-wait loops. Every retry should be justified by something newly observed.

CRITICAL - Lock/unlock workflow:
1. browser_lock requires an existing browser tab - you CANNOT call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; before browser_navigate
2. Correct order: browser_navigate -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;lock&quot; }) -&gt; (interactions) -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;unlock&quot; })
3. If a browser tab already exists (check with browser_tabs list), call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; FIRST before any interactions
4. Only call browser_lock with action: &quot;unlock&quot; when completely done with ALL browser operations for this turn

IMPORTANT - Waiting strategy:
When waiting for page changes, prefer short CDP polling loops with Runtime.evaluate, DOM queries, Page lifecycle signals, or browser_snapshot checks rather than a single long wait.

CDP USAGE:
- Use browser_cdp with a DevTools Protocol method and params object, for example Runtime.evaluate, DOM.getDocument, CSS.getComputedStyleForNode, Profiler.start/stop, Performance.getMetrics, Log.enable, and Network.enable.
- Do not use browser_cdp with CDP Input.* methods. They are denied because they are focus-sensitive in Electron webviews and can route input to Cursor UI instead of the browser page.
- Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for clicks, typing, filling inputs, selecting options, keyboard actions, scrolling, and drag-and-drop.
- Use Runtime.evaluate for advanced DOM-scoped interactions that the dedicated browser tools do not cover.
- For profiling, call Profiler.enable, Profiler.start, reproduce the behavior, then Profiler.stop. The profile is saved to a file and returned as a log_file; read that file only when you need to inspect details.
- For JavaScript evaluation, prefer Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue when possible.
- Device emulation you set with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled, or Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (for example for a phone-sized screenshot) lasts only for the current turn: it is cleared when your turn ends, and the user can reset it from the browser tab at any time. Send Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride yourself once you are done with it within a turn.
- Some browser-wide or sensitive CDP methods are denied, especially cookie, storage, permission, download, target-management, filesystem-backed file-input commands, system-level commands, and CDP navigation/history navigation commands.
- Large CDP responses are saved to files instead of being inlined. Prefer using the returned file path over immediately stuffing large payloads into context; read focused sections only when needed.

VISION:
- browser_take_screenshot attaches an image result that the model can inspect. CDP Page.captureScreenshot returns data inside JSON and should not replace browser_take_screenshot when visual verification is needed.

NOTES:
- browser_snapshot returns snapshot YAML and is the main source of truth for page structure.
- Refs are opaque handles tied to the latest browser_snapshot for that tab.
- Iframe content is not accessible - only elements outside iframes can be interacted with.
- When you stop to report a blocker, include the current page, the target you were trying to reach, the blocker you observed, and the best next action. If the blocker requires manual user interaction, ask the user to take over at that point rather than assuming it in advance." source="mcp" />

<namespace name="cursor" tools="AwaitShell, CreateGoal, Delete, EditNotebook, FetchMcpResource, GenerateImage, ReadLints, SearchConversations, SetActiveBranch, SwitchMode, Task, TodoWrite, UpdateGoal, WebFetch, WebSearch" namespaceUseInstructions="Native Cursor tools for this session. Here are some crucial instructions:
- AwaitShell: Use to sleep and check shell progress. Never sleep using shell.
- ReadLints: Check for linter errors after substantive edits.
- SwitchMode: Switch between modes: Agent and Plan. Proactively consider switching modes for relevant requests.
- Task: Spawn local and cloud subagents natively.
- TodoWrite: Use this tool to manage complex multi-step tasks." source="cursor" />

<namespace name="cursor-ide-browser" tools="browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_mouse_click_xy, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, browser_drag, browser_get_bounding_box, browser_highlight, browser_tabs, browser_cdp, browser_take_screenshot, browser_lock" namespaceUseInstructions="The cursor-ide-browser MCP server provides a Cursor-owned browser tab plus a raw Chrome DevTools Protocol command tool.

CORE WORKFLOW:
1. Start by understanding the user's goal and what success looks like on the page.
2. Use browser_tabs with action &quot;list&quot; to inspect open tabs and URLs before acting.
3. Use browser_navigate to create or navigate the target tab. Omit the position parameter for background automation so focus is preserved.
4. Use browser_lock before longer automation on an existing tab, then browser_lock with action &quot;unlock&quot; when finished.
5. Use browser_snapshot for accessibility context and browser_take_screenshot for visual verification.
6. Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for page interactions.
7. Use browser_highlight and browser_get_bounding_box for visual grounding and coordinate diagnostics.
8. Use browser_cdp for page inspection, profiling, runtime evaluation, DOM/CSS queries, and performance data.

AVOID RABBIT HOLES:
1. Do not repeat the same failing action more than once without new evidence such as a fresh snapshot, a different ref, a changed page state, or a clear new hypothesis.
2. IMPORTANT: If four attempts fail or progress stalls, stop acting and report what you observed, what blocked progress, and the most likely next step.
3. Prefer gathering evidence over brute force. If the page is confusing, use browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot, or CDP inspection before trying more actions.
4. If you encounter a blocker such as login, passkey/manual user interaction, permissions, captchas, destructive confirmations, missing data, or an unexpected state, stop and report it instead of improvising repeated actions.
5. Do not get stuck in wait-action-wait loops. Every retry should be justified by something newly observed.

CRITICAL - Lock/unlock workflow:
1. browser_lock requires an existing browser tab - you CANNOT call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; before browser_navigate
2. Correct order: browser_navigate -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;lock&quot; }) -&gt; (interactions) -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;unlock&quot; })
3. If a browser tab already exists (check with browser_tabs list), call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; FIRST before any interactions
4. Only call browser_lock with action: &quot;unlock&quot; when completely done with ALL browser operations for this turn

IMPORTANT - Waiting strategy:
When waiting for page changes, prefer short CDP polling loops with Runtime.evaluate, DOM queries, Page lifecycle signals, or browser_snapshot checks rather than a single long wait.

CDP USAGE:
- Use browser_cdp with a DevTools Protocol method and params object, for example Runtime.evaluate, DOM.getDocument, CSS.getComputedStyleForNode, Profiler.start/stop, Performance.getMetrics, Log.enable, and Network.enable.
- Do not use browser_cdp with CDP Input.* methods. They are denied because they are focus-sensitive in Electron webviews and can route input to Cursor UI instead of the browser page.
- Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for clicks, typing, filling inputs, selecting options, keyboard actions, scrolling, and drag-and-drop.
- Use Runtime.evaluate for advanced DOM-scoped interactions that the dedicated browser tools do not cover.
- For profiling, call Profiler.enable, Profiler.start, reproduce the behavior, then Profiler.stop. The profile is saved to a file and returned as a log_file; read that file only when you need to inspect details.
- For JavaScript evaluation, prefer Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue when possible.
- Device emulation you set with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled, or Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (for example for a phone-sized screenshot) lasts only for the current turn: it is cleared when your turn ends, and the user can reset it from the browser tab at any time. Send Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride yourself once you are done with it within a turn.
- Some browser-wide or sensitive CDP methods are denied, especially cookie, storage, permission, download, target-management, filesystem-backed file-input commands, system-level commands, and CDP navigation/history navigation commands.
- Large CDP responses are saved to files instead of being inlined. Prefer using the returned file path over immediately stuffing large payloads into context; read focused sections only when needed.

VISION:
- browser_take_screenshot attaches an image result that the model can inspect. CDP Page.captureScreenshot returns data inside JSON and should not replace browser_take_screenshot when visual verification is needed.

NOTES:
- browser_snapshot returns snapshot YAML and is the main source of truth for page structure.
- Refs are opaque handles tied to the latest browser_snapshot for that tab.
- Iframe content is not accessible - only elements outside iframes can be interacted with.
- When you stop to report a blocker, include the current page, the target you were trying to reach, the blocker you observed, and the best next action. If the blocker requires manual user interaction, ask the user to take over at that point rather than assuming it in advance." source="mcp" />

Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. Use when searching for a keyword or file and not confident you'll find the match quickly.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- cursor-guide: Read Cursor product documentation to answer questions about how Cursor Desktop, IDE, CLI, Cloud Agents, Bugbot, and other features work. Use when the user asks 'In Cursor, how do I...?' or similar questions about Cursor products.
- ci-investigator: Investigate a single failing PR CI check and return a short root-cause summary. Use when the user asks to summarize, explain, diagnose, or investigate a specific failed check from a pull request.
- bugbot: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a Bugbot-like review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Bugbot". Launch exactly one Bugbot subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\", \"natural language\">\nChange Description: ...\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Change Description` only when `Diff` is `natural language`, formatting it as one block per changed file (a `<path> (added|modified|deleted|renamed)` header followed by bullets of what changed, mentioning line numbers or ranges inline where helpful), and only use `natural language` as a last resort after a regular diff-based review failed because the diff could not be computed; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- security-review: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a security review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Security Review". Launch exactly one security-review subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- best-of-n-runner: Run a task in an isolated git worktree. Each best-of-n-runner gets its own branch and working directory. Use for best-of-N parallel attempts or isolated experiments.

<dynamic_tools>
You have access to tools through dynamic namespaces, e.g. MCP servers, using `GetDynamicTools` and `CallDynamicTool`.

## Dynamic Tool Discovery and Invocation

Use `GetDynamicTools` to discover tool schemas, then `CallDynamicTool` to invoke one tool. Aim to minimize round-trips: ideally one discovery call followed by one invocation.

If the user mentions a product or service represented by an available namespace, and the request likely depends on it, proactively inspect that namespace before answering. If you are unsure which namespace matches, search with a relevant pattern.

`GetDynamicTools` supports these modes:

1. `{"namespace":"<id>"}`: returns schemas and full descriptions for every tool in that namespace.
2. `{"namespace":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}`: returns one tool schema with its full description.
3. `{"pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches namespace and tool names.
4. `{"namespace":"<id>","pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches tools within one namespace.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions, marked by a trailing "... [truncated]"; namespace and single-tool lookups always return the complete description.

Always inspect a tool's schema before invoking it with `CallDynamicTool`.

If the available dynamic tools do not fully support what the user asked you to do, complete the work you can with the current tool set. In your work summary, include what you were unable to do and why. Do not use browser automation to work around missing tools unless the user explicitly asks you to use the browser.

2. IMPORTANT: If four attempts fail or progress stalls, stop acting and report what you observed, what blocked progress, and the most likely next step.
3. Prefer gathering evidence over brute force. If the page is confusing, use browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot, or CDP inspection before trying more actions.
4. If you encounter a blocker such as login, passkey/manual user interaction, permissions, captchas, destructive confirmations, missing data, or an unexpected state, stop and report it instead of improvising repeated actions.
5. Do not get stuck in wait-action-wait loops. Every retry should be justified by something newly observed.

CRITICAL - Lock/unlock workflow:
1. browser_lock requires an existing browser tab - you CANNOT call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; before browser_navigate
2. Correct order: browser_navigate -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;lock&quot; }) -&gt; (interactions) -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;unlock&quot; })
3. If a browser tab already exists (check with browser_tabs list), call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; FIRST before any interactions
4. Only call browser_lock with action: &quot;unlock&quot; when completely done with ALL browser operations for this turn

IMPORTANT - Waiting strategy:
When waiting for page changes, prefer short CDP polling loops with Runtime.evaluate, DOM queries, Page lifecycle signals, or browser_snapshot checks rather than a single long wait.

CDP USAGE:
- Use browser_cdp with a DevTools Protocol method and params object, for example Runtime.evaluate, DOM.getDocument, CSS.getComputedStyleForNode, Profiler.start/stop, Performance.getMetrics, Log.enable, and Network.enable.
- Do not use browser_cdp with CDP Input.* methods. They are denied because they are focus-sensitive in Electron webviews and can route input to Cursor UI instead of the browser page.
- Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for clicks, typing, filling inputs, selecting options, keyboard actions, scrolling, and drag-and-drop.
- Use Runtime.evaluate for advanced DOM-scoped interactions that the dedicated browser tools do not cover.
- For profiling, call Profiler.enable, Profiler.start, reproduce the behavior, then Profiler.stop. The profile is saved to a file and returned as a log_file; read that file only when you need to inspect details.
- For JavaScript evaluation, prefer Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue when possible.
- Device emulation you set with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled, or Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (for example for a phone-sized screenshot) lasts only for the current turn: it is cleared when your turn ends, and the user can reset it from the browser tab at any time. Send Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride yourself once you are done with it within a turn.
- Some browser-wide or sensitive CDP methods are denied, especially cookie, storage, permission, download, target-management, filesystem-backed file-input commands, system-level commands, and CDP navigation/history navigation commands.
- Large CDP responses are saved to files instead of being inlined. Prefer using the returned file path over immediately stuffing large payloads into context; read focused sections only when needed.

VISION:
- browser_take_screenshot attaches an image result that the model can inspect. CDP Page.captureScreenshot returns data inside JSON and should not replace browser_take_screenshot when visual verification is needed.

NOTES:
- browser_snapshot returns snapshot YAML and is the main source of truth for page structure.
- Refs are opaque handles tied to the latest browser_snapshot for that tab.
- Iframe content is not accessible - only elements outside iframes can be interacted with.
- When you stop to report a blocker, include the current page, the target you were trying to reach, the blocker you observed, and the best next action. If the blocker requires manual user interaction, ask the user to take over at that point rather than assuming it in advance." source="mcp" />

<available_subagent_types>
Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. Use when searching for a keyword or file and not confident you'll find the match quickly.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- cursor-guide: Read Cursor product documentation to answer questions about how Cursor Desktop, IDE, CLI, Cloud Agents, Bugbot, and other features work. Use when the user asks 'In Cursor, how do I...?' or similar questions about Cursor products.
- ci-investigator: Investigate a single failing PR CI check and return a short root-cause summary. Use when the user asks to summarize, explain, diagnose, or investigate a specific failed check from a pull request.
- bugbot: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a Bugbot-like review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Bugbot". Launch exactly one Bugbot subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\", \"natural language\">\nChange Description: ...\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Change Description` only when `Diff` is `natural language`, formatting it as one block per changed file (a `<path> (added|modified|deleted|renamed)` header followed by bullets of what changed, mentioning line numbers or ranges inline where helpful), and only use `natural language` as a last resort after a regular diff-based review failed because the diff could not be computed; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- security-review: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a security review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Security Review". Launch exactly one security-review subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\">\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- best-of-n-runner: Run a task in an isolated git worktree. Each best-of-n-runner gets its own branch and working directory. Use for best-of-N parallel attempts or isolated experiments.
</available_subagent_types>

<dynamic_tools>
You have access to tools through dynamic namespaces, e.g. MCP servers, using `GetDynamicTools` and `CallDynamicTool`.

## Dynamic Tool Discovery and Invocation

Use `GetDynamicTools` to discover tool schemas, then `CallDynamicTool` to invoke one tool. Aim to minimize round-trips: ideally one discovery call followed by one invocation.

If the user mentions a product or service represented by an available namespace, and the request likely depends on it, proactively inspect that namespace before answering. If you are unsure which namespace matches, search with a relevant pattern.

`GetDynamicTools` supports these modes:

1. `{"namespace":"<id>"}`: returns schemas and full descriptions for every tool in that namespace.
2. `{"namespace":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}`: returns one tool schema with its full description.
3. `{"pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches namespace and tool names.
4. `{"namespace":"<id>","pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches tools within one namespace.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions, marked by a trailing "... [truncated]"; namespace and single-tool lookups always return the complete description.

Always inspect a tool's schema before invoking it with `CallDynamicTool`.

If the available dynamic tools do not fully support what the user asked you to do, complete the work you can with the current tool set. In your work summary, include what you were unable to do and why. Do not use browser automation to work around missing tools unless the user explicitly asks you to use the browser.

Available dynamic tool namespaces:

CORE WORKFLOW:
1. Start by understanding the user's goal and what success looks like on the page.
2. Use browser_tabs with action &quot;list&quot; to inspect open tabs and URLs before acting.
3. Use browser_navigate to create or navigate the target tab. Omit the position parameter for background automation so focus is preserved.
4. Use browser_lock before longer automation on an existing tab, then browser_lock with action &quot;unlock&quot; when finished.
5. Use browser_snapshot for accessibility context and browser_take_screenshot for visual verification.
6. Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for page interactions.
7. Use browser_highlight and browser_get_bounding_box for visual grounding and coordinate diagnostics.
8. Use browser_cdp for page inspection, profiling, runtime evaluation, DOM/CSS queries, and performance data.

AVOID RABBIT HOLES:
1. Do not repeat the same failing action more than once without new evidence such as a fresh snapshot, a different ref, a changed page state, or a clear new hypothesis.
2. IMPORTANT: If four attempts fail or progress stalls, stop acting and report what you observed, what blocked progress, and the most likely next step.
3. Prefer gathering evidence over brute force. If the page is confusing, use browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot, or CDP inspection before trying more actions.
4. If you encounter a blocker such as login, passkey/manual user interaction, permissions, captchas, destructive confirmations, missing data, or an unexpected state, stop and report it instead of improvising repeated actions.
5. Do not get stuck in wait-action-wait loops. Every retry should be justified by something newly observed.

CRITICAL - Lock/unlock workflow:
1. browser_lock requires an existing browser tab - you CANNOT call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; before browser_navigate
2. Correct order: browser_navigate -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;lock&quot; }) -&gt; (interactions) -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;unlock&quot; })
3. If a browser tab already exists (check with browser_tabs list), call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; FIRST before any interactions
4. Only call browser_lock with action: &quot;unlock&quot; when completely done with ALL browser operations for this turn

IMPORTANT - Waiting strategy:
When waiting for page changes, prefer short CDP polling loops with Runtime.evaluate, DOM queries, Page lifecycle signals, or browser_snapshot checks rather than a single long wait.

CDP USAGE:
- Use browser_cdp with a DevTools Protocol method and params object, for example Runtime.evaluate, DOM.getDocument, CSS.getComputedStyleForNode, Profiler.start/stop, Performance.getMetrics, Log.enable, and Network.enable.
- Do not use browser_cdp with CDP Input.* methods. They are denied because they are focus-sensitive in Electron webviews and can route input to Cursor UI instead of the browser page.
- Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for clicks, typing, filling inputs, selecting options, keyboard actions, scrolling, and drag-and-drop.
- Use Runtime.evaluate for advanced DOM-scoped interactions that the dedicated browser tools do not cover.
- For profiling, call Profiler.enable, Profiler.start, reproduce the behavior, then Profiler.stop. The profile is saved to a file and returned as a log_file; read that file only when you need to inspect details.
- For JavaScript evaluation, prefer Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue when possible.
- Device emulation you set with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled, or Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (for example for a phone-sized screenshot) lasts only for the current turn: it is cleared when your turn ends, and the user can reset it from the browser tab at any time. Send Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride yourself once you are done with it within a turn.
- Some browser-wide or sensitive CDP methods are denied, especially cookie, storage, permission, download, target-management, filesystem-backed file-input commands, system-level commands, and CDP navigation/history navigation commands.
- Large CDP responses are saved to files instead of being inlined. Prefer using the returned file path over immediately stuffing large payloads into context; read focused sections only when needed.

VISION:
- browser_take_screenshot attaches an image result that the model can inspect. CDP Page.captureScreenshot returns data inside JSON and should not replace browser_take_screenshot when visual verification is needed.

NOTES:
- browser_snapshot returns snapshot YAML and is the main source of truth for page structure.
- Refs are opaque handles tied to the latest browser_snapshot for that tab.
- Iframe content is not accessible - only elements outside iframes can be interacted with.
- When you stop to report a blocker, include the current page, the target you were trying to reach, the blocker you observed, and the best next action. If the blocker requires manual user interaction, ask the user to take over at that point rather than assuming it in advance." source="mcp" />

对话：最终绝杀-收尾-最终收尾
会话ID：01a18c6e-765c-7ae1-8d21-a2f6e1086df2
来源：C:\Users\Kay kay\.codex\archived_sessions\rollout-2026-10-30T18-50-11-01a18c6e-765c-7ae1-8d21-a2f6e1086df2.jsonl 第 8878 行
------------------------------------------------------------------------
已完成这一轮只读排查，**没有修改代码、编译、烧录或操作设备**。

目前最需要优先关注的是：**显示断供、换帧无限等待、页面生命周期冲突**。蓝屏可能有不同原因，不能全部归结为拖动图标。

1. **换帧等待没有真正的超时退出——明确隐患。**  
   显示驱动等待换帧完成时，等待超过 500 次只打印提示，随后继续无限等待。该路径持有界面锁，一旦帧完成事件丢失，整个界面可能一直卡住。[代码位置](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/graphics/lvgl/lvgl/src/drivers/nuttx/lv_nuttx_fbdev.c:330>)

2. **显示 DMA 依赖逐帧中断续传——高风险路径。**  
   当前驱动在一帧完成后，通过中断重新启动下一帧。中断被长时间阻塞、DMA 异常或外部内存供数不足，都可能造成显示断供。ESP32-P4 的 MIPI 屏确实可能因此显示纯蓝，但尚不能证明你遇到的每次蓝屏都是这个原因。[驱动代码](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_mipi_dsi.c:300>)；[乐鑫说明](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-faq/en/latest/software-framework/peripherals/lcd.html)

3. **Flash 擦写期间的显示保护有覆盖上限。**  
   当前使用 64 帧 DMA 链维持显示。如果停缓存、双核同步或 Flash 操作异常延长，保护仍可能耗尽。这属于剩余风险，已有采样没有证明它实际触发过。[代码位置](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_mipi_dsi.c:1715>)

4. **重复打开同一个 APP，可能让旧页面清掉新页面状态。**  
   启动流程先创建新页面，再卸载旧页面；定位、天气等页面使用全局界面指针，卸载回调没有核对页面实例。连续语音打开同一 APP、快速重复启动时，旧回调可能删除新定时器、清空新指针，留下异常状态。[启动流程](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/metalio/display/screen/home_screen/home_screen.cxx:1000>)；[定位卸载逻辑](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/metalio/display/screen/gps_screen/gps_screen.cxx:2078>)

5. **定位任务存在资源释放不完整的路径。**  
   部分任务直接调用 `vTaskDelete()`，这里实际转为 `pthread_exit()`；当前没有 C++ 异常展开，会跳过调用栈中部分字符串等局部对象的析构。反复定位、刷新地图可能逐渐泄漏内存，增加后续分配失败、卡死的风险。[代码位置](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/metalio/display/screen/gps_screen/gps_screen.cxx:1478>)

6. **界面线程仍存在无期限等待后台任务的路径。**  
   水平仪、磁场页面退出时会同步等待传感器线程结束；如果底层通信卡住，界面也会被拖住。另外，显示锁接口虽然接收超时参数，实际上忽略该参数。这些是卡死隐患，尚未证实造成了你的蓝屏。

7. **内存、栈和异常恢复的诊断保护不足。**  
   当前未开启栈染色、栈用量记录、部分 LVGL 对象检查，也未启用硬件看门狗。它们本身不是蓝屏根因，但会让越界、资源耗尽或死锁更难及时定位，故障后也可能长期停留在异常画面。

8. **硬件版本兼容性仍需保留为待查项。**  
   已保存的开机日志识别到芯片为 v1.0，而当前 NuttX 明确提示其完整支持范围是更新版本，并通过配置允许继续启动。这个警告不能直接判定硬件有问题，但不能忽略。[开机日志](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/output/flash_hios/20261102-152349-732376/boot.log:4>)

还有两点必须说明：

- **文件夹拖入后曾有一次串口、心跳同时停止，根因仍未确认。** 后来的压力测试通过，不能据此把这次故障宣布为彻底解决。[故障记录](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/output/folder-merge/failed-fast-drag-device/failure.json>)
- **现有验证存在盲区和版本记录不一致。** 内存截图正常不等于实体屏正常；欠载计数依赖中断执行，中断停住时计数也可能不更新。另外，最新烧录记录、根目录固件和版本状态文件的哈希不同，后续诊断必须对应同一份固件。

历史上已经确认过的“分页重建访问旧控件”“把复合图标当图片对象写入”等问题，当前代码已有防护，我没有将它们重复算成新发现。

**以上是目前有代码或日志依据的隐患清单；只读分析还不能保证穷尽所有原因，也尚未确定你当前蓝屏的唯一根因。**

**可行，可以做成 HiOS 和独立播放器各有一个切换按钮，点击后重启进入另一个固件。** 播放器单独编译成一个 `.bin`，拥有自己的界面、驱动和播放功能。

我只读查看了现有项目，结论如下。

1. **两个系统中的按钮都能实现。**

   HiOS 中增加“进入播放器”，播放器中增加“返回 HiOS”。点击后，保存必要设置、停止播放和存储访问、记录下次启动目标，再重启设备。切换过程中会短暂黑屏，需要重新启动，不能按应用切换的速度来预期。

2. **需要改造启动机制，不能只增加一个播放器 bin。**

   当前 HiOS 配置是 NuttX 的 `Simple Boot`，固件从 Flash 的 `0x2000` 启动，没有现成的双固件选择机制。

   建议结构是：**启动管理器 → 根据选择启动 HiOS 或播放器**。两个按钮负责写入启动选择，由启动管理器完成加载，并提供按键强制返回 HiOS 的恢复入口。

   这意味着 HiOS 也需要修改并重新编译，用来加入按钮和适配启动方式。项目中原厂固件虽然已有双系统切换代码，但不能直接套到当前 HiOS 上。

3. **存储空间初步够用，内存卡也可以共用。**

   项目记录已验证硬件为 **32 MiB Flash**，当前正式 HiOS 固件约 **15.86 MiB**，有规划双固件的空间。不过，具体分区还要结合播放器最终体积、启动管理器和现有设置保留区确定。

   两边可以分别挂载同一张内存卡、读取同一目录的视频。因为重启后只有一个系统运行，不会同时争用文件。首版建议沿用当前已经支持的 FAT32 文件系统。

4. **独立播放器有利于优化，但“直播非常流畅”需要限定视频源。**

   独立固件可以省去语音识别、AI 服务等后台负担，把资源集中在读取、解码、声音和显示上。

   但 ESP32-P4 的 H.264 硬件功能是**编码**，播放 H.264 主要依赖软件解码。乐鑫给出的参考数据中，720p 软件解码约为 10 帧/秒，因此不能承诺普通 720p、1080p 直播稳定达到 25～30 帧/秒。[乐鑫官方说明](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-techpedia/en/latest/esp-friends/solution-introduction/multimedia/component-description/esp-h264.html)

   比较合理的首轮验证目标是 **480×272、H.264 Baseline、25～30 帧/秒**，这只是测试目标，尚未实测。m3u8 是播放列表，能否流畅还取决于里面视频的编码、分辨率、码率和网络状况。只有高清档位的直播，可能需要外部转码才能流畅观看；把画面缩小显示，本身不会省掉高清解码的工作。

**所以，你提出的“双独立固件＋两边按钮互相切换”在架构上可行；主要工作是启动兼容改造，主要性能限制是视频解码。** 后续最值得先验证的是独立播放器对实际本地视频和直播源的播放能力，再确定双系统分区。

本次仅做了只读分析，没有修改文件、编译或烧录设备。

2026-11-02T18:11:29+08:00 | 助手结论
对话：Hi 播
会话ID：01a19bb7-0ae0-74e2-b898-7ec6ad30411e
来源：C:\Users\Kay kay\.codex\archived_sessions\rollout-2026-11-02T18-03-46-01a19bb7-0ae0-74e2-b898-7ec6ad30411e.jsonl 第 98 行
------------------------------------------------------------------------
**可行，而且我更建议直接合入 HiOS，做成原生播放器。** 打开就播放、退出回到桌面，不需要重启。只要播放时合理管理后台任务，独立固件并不一定比它明显更快。

但你最在意的是“流畅不卡顿”，解决重点是**视频编码、解码能力和播放管线**，仅仅合入固件无法解决这些问题。

我看了当前代码：项目里已经有本地视频和 m3u8 播放基础，但目前使用软件 H.264 解码，限制为 Baseline、最大 640×368，并建议使用 480×272、15 帧视频。**这是现有实现的兼容范围，不代表已经达到流畅播放验收。** 15 帧即使不缓冲，运动画面也会有明显的不连贯。

比较好的解决方法有三种：

1. **设备直接播放：方便，但需要选择合适的视频源。**

   本地视频提前转换为低分辨率 H.264 Baseline；直播优先选择兼容的低清档位。播放器内部改成“读取预缓冲 → 解码 → 显示”流水线，让下载和解码尽量重叠，减少逐段读取带来的等待；播放时暂停语音唤醒等非必要计算，并减少画面复制和界面重绘。

   可以争取在较低分辨率下达到稳定的 25～30 帧，但具体分辨率必须实测。增加缓存能吸收网络波动，**无法解决解码速度长期低于视频帧率的问题**。

2. **本地视频使用 MJPEG：更值得优先验证的流畅播放路线。**

   ESP32-P4 有硬件 JPEG 解码能力，MJPEG 视频可以利用它，把连续画面的解码负担从 CPU 转移出去。乐鑫的多媒体框架明确支持 P4 的 MJPEG 硬件解码，而 H.264 解码仍采用软件。[乐鑫官方说明](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-gmf/en/latest/gmf-framework/gmf-elements/gmf-video.html)

   因此，本地视频可以在电脑上提前转成适配的 MJPEG 文件，放进内存卡，由 HiOS 播放。这条路线更有希望获得稳定帧率，代价是**文件体积更大**，需要适配硬件解码、封装读取和音画同步。它不是简单换一个扩展名，也还没有在当前 HiOS 上完成验证。

3. **直播通过转码服务适配：最容易控制流畅度。**

   用电脑、NAS 或服务器读取原始 m3u8，实时转换成设备能稳定处理的视频，再发送给 HiOS。

   可以输出低分辨率 H.264，继续走 m3u8；也可以输出 MJPEG 配合音频，走硬件 JPEG 解码。后一种需要自定义适配的播放传输方式，带宽通常也更大。用户仍可粘贴原始直播地址，但实际由转码服务处理，设备需要连接该服务。

**针对你的目标，我推荐“HiOS 原生播放器＋两条播放路径”：**

- **本地视频：**优先验证硬件 MJPEG，保留兼容 H.264 文件播放。
- **线上直播：**兼容的低清 m3u8 直接播，其余通过转码服务适配。
- **播放模式：**集中资源用于音视频，退出后恢复正常后台功能。

如果要求**不转换文件、不依赖外部服务，直接流畅播放各种原始高清 m3u8**，这块硬件无法可靠保证。P4 缺少 H.264 硬件解码，乐鑫提供的参考性能是 720p 软件解码约 10 帧/秒。[官方性能参考](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-techpedia/en/latest/esp-friends/solution-introduction/multimedia/component-description/esp-h264.html)

下一步应该先在 HiOS 内测出“持续解码并显示 25～30 帧、声音不断、直播分段切换不停顿”的实际能力，再确定默认格式和画质。**先把播放性能做实，再完善播放器界面。** 本次仍仅分析，没有修改或烧录。

那ESP31怎么就能流畅的播放视频？

========================================================================
2026-11-02T18:13:22+08:00 | 助手结论
对话：Hi 播
会话ID：01a19bb7-0ae0-74e2-b898-7ec6ad30411e
来源：C:\Users\Kay kay\.codex\archived_sessions\rollout-2026-11-02T18-03-46-01a19bb7-0ae0-74e2-b898-7ec6ad30411e.jsonl 第 126 行
------------------------------------------------------------------------
**能流畅播放是有依据的，你这块 P4 也有实现流畅播放的潜力。我前面把现有播放器的限制和硬件能力说得太接近了，需要修正：当前代码建议的 15 帧，不是 P4 的性能上限。**

你说的“ESP31”如果是 **ESP32-S31**，乐鑫官方播放器给出了这些参考成绩：

- S31 播放 **H.264：320×240，55 帧/秒**。
- P4 播放 **H.264：320×240，68 帧/秒**。
- P4 播放 **MJPEG：640×480，67 帧/秒；1280×720，25 帧/秒**。

其中 H.264 使用软件解码，S31 和 P4 的 MJPEG 使用硬件解码。这些是官方测试环境下的最大性能，并非当前 HiOS 的实测结果。[官方播放器性能数据](https://components.espressif.com/components/espressif/esp_player/versions/1.0.5/readme)

所以，其他设备能流畅播放，关键要看三个条件：

1. **实际解码的分辨率。** 320×240 的视频放大到全屏，仍然只需解码 320×240；原始 720p 视频缩小显示，则仍需解码全部 720p 数据。
2. **视频编码。** MJPEG 可以用硬件加速；H.264 的解码负担还受编码参数、画面复杂度影响。外观相似的视频，处理难度可能差很多。
3. **播放器实现和运行配置。** 官方测试的 P4 使用 CPU 400 MHz、PSRAM 250 MHz；你当前 HiOS 配置是 CPU 360 MHz、PSRAM 80 MHz，播放器实现也不同，成绩不能直接照搬。[官方测试条件](https://components.espressif.com/components/espressif/esp_player/versions/1.0.5/readme)

**这也意味着，我会调整对你这个项目的建议：先做好设备直接播放，再根据实测决定哪些直播需要转码。** 不应一开始就认定必须依赖外部转码服务。

具体方向是评估移植乐鑫官方 `esp_player` 或复用其解码、缓存和音画同步方案。它已经支持本地文件、HTTP 和 HLS；但面向 ESP-IDF，合入当前 NuttX 版 HiOS 需要适配，不能直接替换一个库就完成。[官方组件说明](https://components.espressif.com/components/espressif/esp_player/versions/1.0.5/readme)

你说的是 **ESP32-S31，还是 ESP32-S3**？如果有你看到的播放器项目或演示链接，发给我，我可以对照它的实际格式、分辨率和实现，判断能否把同样的效果做到 HiOS 中。

**你这块板子有提速空间，但不能直接按“CPU 400 MHz＋PSRAM 250 MHz”作为稳定升级目标。目前更合理的方向是：CPU 保持 360 MHz，优先验证 PSRAM 200 MHz。** :codex-annotation{index="1"}

我前面引用官方播放器测试配置时，没有充分区分 P4 的芯片版本，这里更正。

只读核查发现：

- 保存的设备启动日志明确显示：**ESP32-P4 v1.0**。
- 当前 HiOS 配置：**CPU 360 MHz、PSRAM 80 MHz**。
- 同项目中原厂 ESP-IDF 固件配置：**CPU 360 MHz、PSRAM 200 MHz**。这说明 200 MHz 值得验证，但不能代替当前 HiOS 的实机稳定性测试。

**CPU 升到 400 MHz：有条件，当前不能认定可行。**

乐鑫对 v3.0 以前的芯片，把强制 400 MHz 标为实验功能，并明确要求芯片经过额外资格验证、向乐鑫确认适用。我们目前没有你这颗芯片符合条件的证据，当前 HiOS 的配置也限制旧版芯片选择 400 MHz。[乐鑫官方配置说明](https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/v5.5.4/components/esp_system/port/soc/esp32p4/Kconfig.cpu)

即使能稳定运行，360→400 MHz 的频率提升也只有约 **11%**，不会让视频性能翻倍。

**PSRAM 升到 250 MHz：不属于这颗 v1.0 的官方支持配置。**

乐鑫官方明确将 250 MHz 选项限制为 **v3.0 及以后版本**；旧版可以选择 200 MHz。因此，不能通过取消旧版芯片选项来获得真实的硬件支持。[乐鑫官方 PSRAM 配置](https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/v5.5.4/components/esp_psram/esp32p4/Kconfig.spiram)

另外，我看到当前 HiOS 的底层适配没有明确接通 250 MHz 配置，所以即使菜单显示这个选项，也不能证明实际会按 250 MHz 运行。

**PSRAM 升到 200 MHz：是最值得继续研究的方案。**

它有官方配置支持，也与项目里的原厂固件配置一致。后续若实施，应先核对初始化和时序校准，再验证实际时钟、内存读写正确性，以及屏幕、音频、Wi-Fi 同时工作时的稳定性。

从 80→200 MHz，频率是原来的 **2.5 倍**，但实际内存吞吐和视频帧率不会等比例增长。它更可能改善视频帧读取、颜色转换和显示搬运；如果主要瓶颈在 H.264 解码计算，还需要优化播放器。

**我的建议是先验证“360 MHz CPU＋200 MHz PSRAM”，同时优化播放管线。** 这是现有硬件上更有依据的提升路线；流畅度最终用同一段视频的持续帧率、丢帧和音频连续性来判断。

本次只读取了配置、源码和已有日志，没有修改、编译或操作设备。

2026-11-03T11:31:33+08:00 | 助手结论
对话：终极必杀-全面提升—全面升级
会话ID：01a15d27-04ea-7bb2-891c-93ff6c12fc12
来源：C:\Users\Kay kay\.codex\sessions\2026\10\26\rollout-2026-10-26T11-06-09-01a15d27-04ea-7bb2-891c-93ff6c12fc12_01a1762c-2d26-72c1-b469-88cfaa355330.jsonl 第 42287 行
------------------------------------------------------------------------
目前优先怀疑的是**电台在 4G 下的连接、缓冲和超时退出流程**。代码中发现了三处相关问题：

1. **HLS 分段电台的取消机制不完整。** MP3 已接入可取消连接，HLS 没有接入同一套机制。网络请求卡住后，即使触发超时，播放器仍可能停在等待退出、重建连接的阶段，界面就一直显示“连接中”。

2. **缓冲要求与连接超时存在冲突。** HLS 要积累约 **10 秒音频**才开始出声，但启动超时是 **20 秒**。4G 下载较慢时，可能尚未攒够缓冲就开始重试，已有缓冲又被清空。

3. **换网后旧连接缺少明确的重建机制。** 从 WiFi 切到 4G 后，已有连接可能仍关联旧网络，持续连接和分段下载会受到影响。

另外，“连接中”直到音频真正进入播放队列才消失，因此它也可能表示正在等待缓冲，并不一定还在建立网络连接。

**目前尚不能确定你这次具体卡在哪一步。** 电脑当前未检测到设备串口，没有抓到这次故障的现场日志。以上是代码中确认存在的风险点；这轮没有改代码、切网或烧录。

这是一个叫 **HiOS 的嵌入式智能终端系统项目**，主要运行在 **ESP32-P4 的 Metalio Claw4 硬件**上。可以把它理解成：给一台带触摸屏的小设备做操作系统、桌面、AI 助手和配套应用。

从代码和当前配置来看：

- **系统底层**：基于 **openvela / Apache NuttX**，使用 C/C++，当前配置开启了双核 SMP。
- **图形界面**：使用 **LVGL 9.5**，包含桌面、控制中心、后台管理、主题和中文输入法。
- **AI 能力**：有语音唤醒、音频处理、联网对话、数字人、翻译和 AI 生图相关模块。
- **设备功能**：包含 Wi-Fi、4G、短信、电话、摄像头、音乐、GPS、蓝牙和 USB 副屏等代码。
- **应用生态**：支持从 SD 卡安装 `.hiapp` 应用，使用 Lua，并提供受限的 JavaScript 运行能力。目录里已有浏览器、电子书、便签和视频应用。

主要代码可以从这几个位置看：

- [apps/metalio](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/metalio>)：HiOS 的核心应用、界面和服务。
- [nuttx](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/nuttx>)：系统内核、硬件适配和编译配置。
- [external_apps](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/external_apps>)：独立应用、安装包和 SDK 说明。
- [平台说明](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/docs/esp32p4-platform32.md>)：双核、32MB Flash、构建和烧录说明。

**项目已经有较多实现和固件产物，超过了概念演示阶段。** 目录里有 `nuttx.bin`、编译日志和硬件验证说明；文档显示主要构建环境在 Linux / VMware。部分早期验收清单与后续文档进度不一致，因此不能仅凭模块存在就认定所有功能都已在实机上完整通过测试。

它的优势主要在于：**围绕一块嵌入式硬件，做出了比较完整的系统体验，并且留有扩展应用的空间。** 从刚才看到的代码，有这几个亮点：

- **适合资源有限的设备**  
  NuttX + LVGL 这套架构面向嵌入式场景，可以在微控制器上提供触屏界面、多任务和网络服务。实际启动速度、内存占用和续航还需要实测。

- **软硬件整合比较深入**  
  项目覆盖屏幕、触摸、相机、音频、通信、电源和存储，也做了桌面、输入法、设置等公共功能。后续开发应用时，能复用这些基础设施。

- **AI 与设备功能有结合基础**  
  已有本地唤醒、音频处理、联网对话和 MCP 工具分发代码，具备让语音助手调用设备功能的基础。不过，对话体验仍受网络和后端服务影响。

- **支持独立安装应用**  
  `.hiapp` 和 Lua 运行时让浏览器、便签、电子书等应用可以通过 SD 卡安装更新，减少每次增加功能都重新刷固件的需要。这是它从单一固件走向应用平台的一个优势。

- **已经考虑性能和故障处理**  
  双核调度、后台图片处理、超时回退、应用权限与运行预算、设置存储保护等都有实现或说明，体现出对稳定性的考虑。

如果你的目标是做 **AI 桌面终端、智能中控或可定制的小型触屏设备**，这些优势比较有价值。目前最有说服力的是功能整合与可扩展性；性能、功耗和长期稳定性方面，还需要实机数据来证明。

2026-11-03T19:27:07+08:00 | 助手结论
对话：看一下这个是个什么项目。
会话ID：01a1a0f9-e44b-7da2-865b-6c52ad984d82
来源：C:\Users\Kay kay\.codex\archived_sessions\rollout-2026-11-03T18-34-53-01a1a0f9-e44b-7da2-865b-6c52ad984d82.jsonl 第 121 行
------------------------------------------------------------------------
**可以往“小米智能家庭屏”的方向升级。对目前这套 HiOS，我最推荐的路线是：保留 ESP32-P4，先做“家庭中控 + 语音助手 + 家庭信息屏”，再决定是否投入完整影音能力。**

这里先把“小米智慧屏”理解为小米智能家庭屏这类产品。如果你指的是电视级大屏，硬件路线会明显不同。以下只做分析，没有修改项目。

**1. HiOS 已有基础，但几个功能还需要补齐实际链路**

进一步看代码后，比前面介绍能更准确地区分：

- **智能家居已有真实接入基础**：已经能连接 Home Assistant，发送控制请求、读取状态，并处理鉴权失败、离线和执行超时。
- **目前真实绑定主要限于灯和开关**：支持开关、灯光亮度；虽然界面包含窗帘、空调，但未绑定设备时有些操作只是改变本地状态。不能把这些界面当作已经完成的全屋控制。[对应代码](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/metalio/display/screen/smart_home/ha_client.cxx:206>)
- **语音和界面可以继续复用**：已有唤醒、音频处理、对话、MCP，以及桌面、控制中心和输入法。
- **视频能力目前偏轻量**：现有后端限制 H.264 Baseline 最大 640×368，建议 480×272、15fps。适合轻量视频，距离完整影音终端还有差距。[媒体能力说明](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/external_apps/HiApp-Media-SDK-1.txt>)
- **整机 OTA 尚未打通**：有版本检查与界面，但当前固件缺少兼容更新分区，安装会返回失败。[对应代码](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/metalio/ota/ota.cxx:804>)

所以，升级的重点应当是**让现有功能形成可靠、连贯的家庭使用体验**。

**2. 第一优先：把桌面变成“家庭首页”**

现在的应用桌面适合探索功能。家庭屏更需要让人走近就能看到信息、完成操作。

我建议保留原应用桌面，增加可选的“家庭模式”，首页放：

- 时间、天气、室内温湿度。
- 常用设备：客厅灯、空调、窗帘。
- 场景按钮：回家、离家、睡眠、观影。
- 正在播放的音乐、计时器、提醒。
- 空闲时切换时钟或相册，夜间降低亮度。

针对现有 720×720 界面，优先做大按钮、少层级和清晰的设备状态。天气、传感器等数据要明确显示更新时间，断网后避免把旧数据表现为实时数据。

**3. 最重要的能力升级：完整的家庭设备控制**

建议沿用已有 Home Assistant 接入，扩展设备类型和状态管理，减少在 P4 上逐个适配厂商协议的工作。

职责可以这样分：

**HiOS 负责触摸、语音、显示；家庭服务器负责设备接入、自动化和较重的处理。**

Home Assistant 放在 NAS、小主机或常开的电脑上。米家设备可评估小米官方提供的 `xiaomi_home` 集成；它有设备类别和连接方式限制，需要按家里实际型号核对，不能承诺所有米家设备都能接入或离线控制。[小米官方集成说明](https://github.com/XiaoMi/ha_xiaomi_home)

HiOS 端优先补齐：

- 自动读取设备、房间和能力，减少手填实体 ID。
- 空调温度/模式、窗帘位置、传感器和场景执行。
- 设备状态变化及时同步。
- 控制后区分“已发送”“已执行”“失败”。

目前客户端约每两秒逐个轮询设备。设备数量增加后，建议改为订阅状态变化，配合重连和状态补同步；Home Assistant 提供相应 WebSocket 接口。[官方接口文档](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/internals/websocket-api/)

另外，**通过桥接控制米家设备，与获得小爱、米家原生联动、跨屏通话等完整生态能力，是不同范围的工作**，需要分别核实接口和接入条件。

**4. 语音需要从“能聊天”升级到“能可靠办事”**

这部分最能体现智慧屏价值。

例如说“把客厅灯调暗一点”，理想流程应是：识别房间和设备 → 调整亮度 → 等待设备状态确认 → 在屏幕和语音里反馈结果。

建议重点完善：

- 常用家居指令走确定的执行流程，大模型负责理解复杂表达。
- 同名设备能追问：“客厅还是卧室？”
- 播放音乐时能唤醒，交互结束后恢复播放。
- 屏幕持续显示正在听、正在处理、执行结果。
- 联网失败时保留计时器、音量、亮度等本地能力。

**本地唤醒不等于离线语音控制。** 如果要断网也能说“关灯”，还需要本地指令识别，以及不依赖外网的设备控制链路。远场拾音效果则要结合麦克风、音腔和实机声学测试判断。

**5. 影音是需要单独做选择的分界线**

保留当前硬件，可以先做音乐、网络电台、相册、轻量视频，以及经过服务器转换的摄像头画面。

但如果你的目标包括高清追剧、多个摄像头实时预览、流畅视频通话、完整网页和丰富第三方应用，我建议评估带硬件视频解码及更大内存的 Linux／Android 平台。

ESP32-P4 官方标注的 H.264 硬件能力是**编码**，不能据此推断它能直接完成高清硬件解码；当前 HiOS 使用的也是软件解码路径。[乐鑫产品说明](https://www.espressif.com/en/products/socs/esp32-p4)

服务器转码能缓解格式和码率问题，但会增加服务器依赖与延迟。

**6. 我建议按这三个阶段推进**

1. **先验证真实控制链路**  
   选家里实际使用的一盏灯、一台空调、一幅窗帘和一个传感器，验证绑定、触摸控制、语音控制、状态回传及断网恢复。这一步决定方案是否适合你的家庭。

2. **做出可日常使用的家庭屏**  
   增加家庭首页、房间管理、场景、时钟相册、计时提醒和统一语音反馈。验收看实际使用：手机改了设备状态，屏幕能同步；控制失败能说明原因；音乐和语音切换正常。

3. **完善长期运行，再扩影音**  
   补齐可恢复的固件升级、配网与凭据管理、长时间运行稳定性和资源释放。之后根据实测结果决定保留 P4，还是升级主板。

**我的判断：当前 HiOS 最有潜力的定位，是可定制的家庭 AI 中控屏。** 这条路线能复用已有投入，先做出每天用得上的体验；完整影音智慧屏则应作为后续独立评估的目标。

**可以把这三者的能力接入 HiOS，但需要采用“HiOS 终端＋外部计算主机”的方式。当前 ESP32-P4 不能独立运行这些完整模型和服务。**

1. **文章里的视觉问答：可以实现，HiOS 已有基础。**  
   拍照识物、看冰箱推荐菜谱、解释画面、分析设备面板，都可以接入。当前“Hi 视界”已经具备拍照、JPEG 编码、上传图片和接收回答的流程，见 [相机问答代码](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/metalio/display/screen/camera_screen/camera_screen.cxx:2007>)。  
   mPLUG-Owl3-2B 放在电脑或服务器运行，HiOS 调用它。[原文章](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_33481022/article/details/157484684)使用的是带 NVIDIA 显卡的电脑，并不是让微控制器中控屏直接运行模型。

2. **Xiaomi-OCR-0：可以接入，适合扩展成“拍照读文档”。**  
   官方提供文字与文档解析、表格和公式识别、指定字段提取 JSON、文档问答，以及图片/PDF 处理工具。因此可以在 HiOS 上做拍照读字并朗读、提取票据金额、识别说明书、阅读扫描件等功能。[官方说明](https://github.com/xiaomi-research/Xiaomi-OCR-0/blob/main/README_zh.md)  
   **它是 0.8B 模型，仍不适合当前板端直接推理。** 模型、PDF 处理和版面分析应放到外部主机；HiOS 负责采集、显示、交互和保存结果。复杂表格、公式的展示还需要新增界面。

3. **Xiaomi Miloco：可以作为家庭智能后端接入，工程量最大。**  
   可接入的方向包括米家设备查询与控制、摄像头事件、家庭成员识别、家庭记忆、长期任务、主动提醒和场景联动。当前 Miloco 2.0 是运行在 OpenClaw 上的插件，官方要求 macOS/Linux，建议主机内存至少 4GB；默认感知与 Agent 主要依赖云端模型，**不能直接把它理解为全离线方案**。[官方说明](https://github.com/XiaoMi/xiaomi-miloco/blob/main/README.zh.md)  
   HiOS 已有 Home Assistant 设备控制接口，见 [现有家居接口](</C:/Users/Kay kay/Desktop/Hi/HiOS/apps/metalio/display/screen/smart_home/ha_client.h:22>)，但这不等于已经接通 Miloco。还需要适配账号、设备标识、任务和事件回传。HiOS 自带摄像头能否作为 Miloco 感知源，也需要单独适配验证。

实际接入时，可以让 HiOS 的同一个入口按任务调用不同后端：

- **“读一下这张纸”** → Xiaomi-OCR-0。
- **“看看冰箱里能做什么菜”** → 通用视觉模型。
- **“有人进客厅时开灯”** → Miloco 管理感知、任务与设备执行。

还有两个边界：照片中的灯需要与真实设备建立对应关系，才能准确控制；“长时间没移动”“昨天遥控器在哪里”需要连续观测或历史记录，单张照片问答无法完成。

**结论是：三者可以整合成 HiOS 的使用体验，但不能全部塞进当前固件独立运行。** 建议先接通 OCR 和单张图片问答，再接 Miloco 的设备与事件，最后做持续感知和家庭记忆。目前完成的是资料与代码核查，这三项新集成尚未实施或实机验证。

Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. Use when searching for a keyword or file and not confident you'll find the match quickly.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- cursor-guide: Read Cursor product documentation to answer questions about how Cursor Desktop, IDE, CLI, Cloud Agents, Bugbot, and other features work. Use when the user asks 'In Cursor, how do I...?' or similar questions about Cursor products.
- ci-investigator: Investigate a single failing PR CI check and return a short root-cause summary. Use when the user asks to summarize, explain, diagnose, or investigate a specific failed check from a pull request.
- bugbot: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a Bugbot-like review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Bugbot". Launch exactly one Bugbot subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\", \"natural language\">\nChange Description: ...\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Change Description` only when `Diff` is `natural language`, formatting it as one block per changed file (a `<path> (added|modified|deleted|renamed)` header followed by bullets of what changed, mentioning line numbers or ranges inline where helpful), and only use `natural language` as a last resort after a regular diff-based review failed because the diff could not be computed; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- security-review: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a security review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Security Review". Launch exactly one security-review subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\">\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- best-of-n-runner: Run a task in an isolated git worktree. Each best-of-n-runner gets its own branch and working directory. Use for best-of-N parallel attempts or isolated experiments.

<dynamic_tools>
You have access to tools through dynamic namespaces, e.g. MCP servers, using `GetDynamicTools` and `CallDynamicTool`.

## Dynamic Tool Discovery and Invocation

Use `GetDynamicTools` to discover tool schemas, then `CallDynamicTool` to invoke one tool. Aim to minimize round-trips: ideally one discovery call followed by one invocation.

If the user mentions a product or service represented by an available namespace, and the request likely depends on it, proactively inspect that namespace before answering. If you are unsure which namespace matches, search with a relevant pattern.

`GetDynamicTools` supports these modes:

1. `{"namespace":"<id>"}`: returns schemas and full descriptions for every tool in that namespace.
2. `{"namespace":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}`: returns one tool schema with its full description.
3. `{"pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches namespace and tool names.
4. `{"namespace":"<id>","pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches tools within one namespace.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions, marked by a trailing "... [truncated]"; namespace and single-tool lookups always return the complete description.

Always inspect a tool's schema before invoking it with `CallDynamicTool`.

If the available dynamic tools do not fully support what the user asked you to do, complete the work you can with the current tool set. In your work summary, include what you were unable to do and why. Do not use browser automation to work around missing tools unless the user explicitly asks you to use the browser.

AVOID RABBIT HOLES:
1. Do not repeat the same failing action more than once without new evidence such as a fresh snapshot, a different ref, a changed page state, or a clear new hypothesis.
2. IMPORTANT: If four attempts fail or progress stalls, stop acting and report what you observed, what blocked progress, and the most likely next step.

4. If you encounter a blocker such as login, passkey/manual user interaction, permissions, captchas, destructive confirmations, missing data, or an unexpected state, stop and report it instead of improvising repeated actions.
5. Do not get stuck in wait-action-wait loops. Every retry should be justified by something newly observed.

CRITICAL - Lock/unlock workflow:
1. browser_lock requires an existing browser tab - you CANNOT call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; before browser_navigate
2. Correct order: browser_navigate -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;lock&quot; }) -&gt; (interactions) -&gt; browser_lock({ action: &quot;unlock&quot; })
3. If a browser tab already exists (check with browser_tabs list), call browser_lock with action: &quot;lock&quot; FIRST before any interactions
4. Only call browser_lock with action: &quot;unlock&quot; when completely done with ALL browser operations for this turn

IMPORTANT - Waiting strategy:
When waiting for page changes, prefer short CDP polling loops with Runtime.evaluate, DOM queries, Page lifecycle signals, or browser_snapshot checks rather than a single long wait.

CDP USAGE:
- Use browser_cdp with a DevTools Protocol method and params object, for example Runtime.evaluate, DOM.getDocument, CSS.getComputedStyleForNode, Profiler.start/stop, Performance.getMetrics, Log.enable, and Network.enable.
- Do not use browser_cdp with CDP Input.* methods. They are denied because they are focus-sensitive in Electron webviews and can route input to Cursor UI instead of the browser page.
- Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for clicks, typing, filling inputs, selecting options, keyboard actions, scrolling, and drag-and-drop.
- Use Runtime.evaluate for advanced DOM-scoped interactions that the dedicated browser tools do not cover.
- For profiling, call Profiler.enable, Profiler.start, reproduce the behavior, then Profiler.stop. The profile is saved to a file and returned as a log_file; read that file only when you need to inspect details.
- For JavaScript evaluation, prefer Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue when possible.
- Device emulation you set with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled, or Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (for example for a phone-sized screenshot) lasts only for the current turn: it is cleared when your turn ends, and the user can reset it from the browser tab at any time. - Large CDP responses are saved to files instead of being inlined. Prefer using the returned file path over immediately stuffing large payloads into context; read focused sections only when needed.
